_about: Tiny fixtures for combine_witnesses.py. Source only; expected outcomes are the specification. Index convention: A has nA vertices 0..nA-1, B has nB; a pair [i,j] in I means A[i] and B[j] are the SAME point; a pair [i,j] in Ex means A[i] and B[j] are at unit distance.

fixtures.name: F1_4cycle_negative_sample
fixtures.note: The union is the 4-cycle A0-a1-a2(=b2)-b1-A0, which is 2-colourable: A0=1,a1=2,a2=1,b1=2. So 'no witness' here is emphatically NOT non-colourability. The two singleton families clash: the pins force pi(2)=1 (from b0) and pi(2)=3 (from b2).

fixtures.name: F2_4cycle_enlarged_family_succeeds
fixtures.note: Adding phi'=(1,2,1) makes the pins consistent (pi(2)=1 twice); any bijection with pi(2)=1 works, one of which gives cB=(1,2,1). Success is monotone in the families.

fixtures.name: F3_cross_edge_forces_a_nonidentity_permutation
fixtures.note: Pin pi(1)=1; cross edge forbids pi(2)=2; the residual matching must send 2 to 3. Minimal demonstration that forbidden cells are what force a nontrivial permutation.

fixtures.name: F4_duplicate_cross_edge_entry
fixtures.note: A repeated cross edge is rejected rather than silently deduped, because a duplicated entry signals a malformed geometric pipeline upstream. The union here is perfectly colourable; the rejection is about the input, not the maths.

fixtures.name: F5_cross_edge_on_an_identified_pair
fixtures.note: A[1] is identified with B[1] and is also at unit distance from it: (b) demands equal colours and (x) demands unequal. The seed itself is not k-colourable, so no colouring search should be attempted. Note PhiB is improper here too; the seed-level check fires first.

fixtures.name: F6_missing_boundary_entry
fixtures.note: The certified coincidence set contains (2,2) but I omits it. Silently ignoring it would drop a real equation and could manufacture a spurious witness, so the call must fail.

fixtures.name: F7_improper_family_member
fixtures.note: A family member that is not a proper colouring confers no authority: this is the only step that makes the sampled data 'certified'.

fixtures.name: F8_pin_lands_in_a_forbidden_cell
fixtures.note: Pin pi(1)=1 from (A0,B0); the cross edge (A2,B0) forbids (psi(B0),phi(A2))=(1,1), i.e. exactly the pinned cell. So this pair fails at the PIN_FORBIDDEN stage, which the driver reports as a pair-level failure (counted in pair_failures), not a seed rejection.

fixtures.name: F9_bad_index
fixtures.note: Out-of-range index in the identification list; caught before any colouring is looked at.
